extracted.intended_audience: SBIR reviewers, assay developers, biotech commercialization teams, regulators and public-health diagnostics developers
extracted.subtask_description: A Phase I/II SBIR research and commercialization plan to optimize, validate, manufacture, and seek regulatory approval for a rapid, point-of-care HIV incidence assay that discriminates recent vs. long‑term infections. The plan includes explicit analytical performance targets, field evaluations, manufacturing and regulatory strategies, and commercialization considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: False recency rate target
rubrics_metrics.description: Optimization of antibody capture format, detection, dissociation conditions and interpretation criteria to yield <2% false recency compared to LAg ELISA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim 1a explicitly sets the goal: yield <2% false recency compared to LAg ELISA. Aim 2a repeats the ≤2% false recency goal across multiple subtypes and panels. This is the primary performance acceptance criterion for incidence classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correlation with LAg ELISA and validation correlation thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: Achieve >98% correlation with LAg ELISA in prototype/field evaluations and achieve >95% correlation for plasma controls validation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Phase I prototypes yielded >98% correlation with LAg ELISA on a CDC panel. Aim 1b: validation of plasma controls should reach correlation of >95% with standard controls to signal success. Field testing goal is >98% correlation (Aim 1e). Discrepancies are to be investigated and addressed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sensitivity and specificity across subtypes and clinical states
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate sensitivity and specificity of antibody detection and discrimination of recent vs. long-term infections across multiple HIV subtypes and sample types including seroconversion series, long-term infections, elite controllers, and ART-treated individuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim 2a mandates analysis across multiple subtypes using repository and seroconversion panels (DOD, CDC, CEPHIA, Blood Systems Research Institute, SeraCare) with the goal of ≤2% false recency; includes explicit inclusion of varied clinical states to ensure robustness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time-to-result / rapid format requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Deliver a rapid, point-of-care test with time-to-result <15 minutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific Aims and Research Strategy emphasize a rapid (<15 minute) lateral flow format combining titer and avidity analysis suitable for field use, contrasting with ELISA laboratory-based methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ease of use, reproducibility, and clarity of interpretation in field settings
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate device accuracy, ease of use, reproducibility, and clarity of interpretation in resource-limited field sites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim 1e prescribes field testing at four resource-limited sites (CDC and MHRP sites) with 200 sequential unlinked samples each; the device must be usable in low-resource settings and produce reproducible, clear interpretations; discrepancies must be investigated and lead to modifications as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Controls preparation and stability
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare and validate plasma controls (incident, prevalent, negative) using dried tube specimens or lyophilization, with controls showing >95% correlation to standard controls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim 1b: validation involves comparison with standard controls’ ability to detect introduced error; correlation >95% will signal success. Controls must be stable/portable for field use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specimen type equivalence (whole blood vs. plasma)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate a rapid plasma separation device to permit use of whole blood; demonstrate >98% correlation between spun plasma and membrane-separated whole blood.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim 2b: comparison to be performed at Blood Systems Research Institute; the goal is >98% correlation between specimen types to support population surveillance from whole blood in the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design and manufacturing readiness (pilot and scale-up)
rubrics_metrics.description: Design cassette, transfer to manufacturing, produce pilot lots, perform QC, and have capacity for final production in an FDA-registered facility or via qualified contract manufacturers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim 1d and Finance Plan describe manufacturing at Immunetics’ FDA-registered Boston facility (assembly, labeling, QC), maintenance of cold storage and rolling inventory, and plans to contract higher-volume manufacturers if needed; pilot lots must support lab and field evaluations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventory and cold-chain management
rubrics_metrics.description: Post-manufacture product must be sequestered in cold rooms with space reserved to maintain a rolling inventory adequate for 90-day shipments, with provision to expand cold storage as needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Finance Plan specifies available cold room space (400 sf and 200 sf), and the intent to install additional storage if production scales up; this is part of ensuring product quality and supply readiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training materials and instructions for use
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare instructions for use, interpretation spreadsheet and a training package including photographs or video demonstrating test method process and interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim 1c requires simultaneous preparation of user documentation and training aids to support field deployment and consistent interpretation by non-laboratory personnel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field evaluation study design and sample size
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct multi-site field evaluations: four resource-limited sites, each testing 200 sequential unlinked samples in parallel with LAg ELISA or current surveillance method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim 1e defines the study design and sample sizes, sets the >98% correlation target, and requires investigation of discrepant results for iterative assay improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validation using well-characterized panels with closely estimated infection dates
rubrics_metrics.description: Validate final-format test performance using plasma panels with closely estimated HIV infection dates and other relevant sample sets from established repositories (DOD, CDC, CEPHIA, Blood Systems Research Institute, SeraCare).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim 2 lists repositories and panel types to be used for rigorous validation of recency classification performance and cross-subtype behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory submission and approval strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare data for publication and for submission to FDA for waiver of approval to allow intended use for population surveillance, and pursue CE mark and other regulatory approvals as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim 3 explicitly states the regulatory goals (FDA waiver for population surveillance, CE mark, approvals in target countries/regions) and ties assay validation data to regulatory submissions; prior CBER experience is cited as relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory and QA compliance experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate experience with regulatory approval pathways (CBER/FDA) and quality assurance systems necessary for development, manufacture and release of blood screening tests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commercialization narrative cites prior FDA 510(k) approvals (BacTx®, C6 Lyme ELISA) and experience with CBER requirements as a major strength translatable to this project; this is an implied criterion for successful commercialization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novel technical approach and multiplex capability
rubrics_metrics.description: Implement and demonstrate the novel one-step avidity approach, QuickELISA™ capture format, and a highly-sensitive multi-color peroxidase-based detection system enabling ELISA-equivalent sensitivity and multiplexed, visual or simple densitometry readout.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research Strategy and Innovation sections describe three innovations (one-step avidity, QuickELISA capture allowing minimal dilution, and multi-color enzymatic detection with enhanced sensitivity) that are technical requirements/advantages of the proposed product and should be demonstrated during development and validation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analytical equivalence to ELISA sensitivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Achieve detection sensitivity equivalent to ELISA while operating in a lateral flow/rapid test format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Innovation emphasizes ELISA-equivalent sensitivity via the novel detection chemistry; validation must compare performance with ELISA-based gold standards (e.g., LAg ELISA).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of standardized evaluation panels and repositories
rubrics_metrics.description: Include established, standardized panels (e.g., serially collected plasma with closely estimated infection dates) and recognized repository sources for objective validation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific Aims reference using a Phase I collected panel and repositories (CDC, DOD, CEPHIA, Blood Systems Research Institute, SeraCare) — use of these sources provides comparability and credibility for validation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data dissemination and peer-reviewed publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare and publish study data to support scientific credibility and regulatory submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim 3 requires preparing data for publication as part of the path to commercialization and regulatory acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Market positioning and competitiveness (eliminate need for RITA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Design and validate a single, simple, accurate HIV incidence rapid test with false recency equivalent to LAg ELISA to eliminate need for complex RITAs and capture market share rapidly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commercialization Plan argues market advantage by replacing multi-assay RITA approaches, projecting rapid market uptake and TAM share capture within three years; competitive landscape analysis (lack of direct rapid-test competitors) supports this criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellectual property and freedom-to-operate
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess and secure IP protection for proprietary methods (QuickELISA™, multi-color detection), review patent landscape for lateral flow technology, and ensure freedom to operate; note public-domain status of IDR-M antigen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commercialization Plan lists issued patents (7,262,019; 7,125,517; 7,105,311) and patent application 61/494,232; it also notes IDR-M is public domain. Legal counsel availability to resolve freedom-to-operate issues is stated.
